liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): Reviewer notes the last four verses of Saint Stephen appear on the same track as The Eleven [9]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): Reviewer calls the studio version of The Eleven excellent [2]
- **The Barbed Wire Whipping Party** (1 review): Reviewer considers it among the strangest tracks the band ever recorded [2]
- **Whats Become Of The Baby?** (1 review): Reviewer finds it actually listenable here, at times evoking And We Bid You Goodnight [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Barbed Wire Whipping Party**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Unknown Instrumental**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Mountains Of The Moon**: rare: 14 archived performances [14]
- **Whats Become Of The Baby?**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Rosemary**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Mountains Of The Moon**: rare: 14 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd69-xx-xx.sbd.dodd.16760.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 13 songs; 61 min; rated 4.08/5 by 36 [1]. Said about its sound: Rough, preliminary outtakes with some hiss and slight muddiness, yet easier on the ears than the commercial album release; Uploader notes a skip at the beginning of The Eleven, and the jam at its end fades out [1][5]

## Around the show

- Citing McNally, the album's working title was Earthquake Country; sixteen tracks and heavy drug use made sessions a fuzzy quagmire [6]
- Reviewer doubts the band was in the studio on December 31, 1969, suggesting they prepared for a New Year's gig [12]
- Reviewer hears parts resembling an early electric Weather Report Suite Prelude, and other parts like the 'lower down' section of St Stephen [3]
- Less freaky and effects-laden than the released Aoxomoxoa; Rosemary is only slightly less effects-heavy than the album version [5]
- Reviewer says the original Aoxomoxoa mix, remixed in September 1971, is clearly more rambunctious than the remix [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-xx-xx.sbd.dodd.16760.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard - Studio [1]. Also: Reviewer owned this on bootleg vinyl years ago, but that copy lacked some of the pieces; Reviewer's friend once had a tape made from an untitled bootleg LP with a weird hand-drawn cover; Uploader describes cleanup work: removed pops and a small cut near the start of Barbed Wire, with some faint noise left in The Rag [1][8][11]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by gratefuldeadcoverart.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead Aoxomoxoa Outtakes](https://gratefuldeadcoverart.blogspot.com/2013/10/grateful-dead-aoxomoxoa-outtakes.html) [15]
